method: Pearson and Spearman correlation with n printed for every value. The 95% interval is Fisher z. The p-value is a two-sided permutation test with 20,000 shuffles and a fixed seed, so it is reproducible and does not rely on a normality assumption. Only official numbers are used: finals from the NFL schedule pages and the NFL standings page. No price data is involved, so none of these are market correlations.

rows.note: Do scoring-heavy games also blow out? The screen for whether a total and a spread are independent legs of the same ticket.

rows.pair: game total vs signed home margin
rows.note: Directional version of the row above; reported separately so the two cannot be confused (see FLG-22 in COORDINATION.md).

rows.pair: away score vs home score (same game)
rows.note: Within-game co-movement. This is the quantity that decides whether two legs in one game may be multiplied as if independent.

rows.pair: points for per game vs points against per game (clubs)
rows.note: Club-level balance: does scoring more come with allowing more?

rows.pair: net points per game vs win pct (clubs)
rows.note: How much of a club's record its scoring differential already explains.

rows.pair: points for per game vs win pct (clubs)
points against per game vs win pct (clubs)
home win pct vs road win pct (clubs)
rows.note: Is home form portable to the road? If this is weak, 'they play well at home' is not evidence for a road game.

rows.pair: last-5 win pct vs net points per game (clubs)
rows.note: Does the recent record track the underlying point differential, i.e. is 'form' mostly a restatement of quality?
